definition: The compact representation for quasi-Newton methods is a matrix decomposition, which is typically used in gradient based optimization algorithms or for solving nonlinear systems.
details: The decomposition uses a low-rank representation for the direct and/or inverse Hessian or the Jacobian of a nonlinear system. Because of this, the compact representation is often used for large problems and constrained optimization.

explainer.lead: A compact quasi-Newton representation is a space-saving way to describe the matrix approximation used in many optimization and nonlinear-system calculations. Its low-rank form makes it especially useful for large problems and constrained optimization.

tiers.eli5: Imagine trying to improve a huge machine without writing down how every part affects every other part. You keep a short summary of the most important relationships instead. A compact quasi-Newton representation does something similar, helping a computer take useful steps without keeping the whole giant table.
tiers.practitioner: Use the decomposition to represent a direct or inverse Hessian, or a Jacobian, through low-rank factors rather than an explicit full matrix. It fits gradient-based optimization, nonlinear-system solving, and large or constrained problems. Remember that it is a matrix representation: the approximation can concern the Hessian, its inverse, or a Jacobian, depending on the calculation.
tiers.paperLevel: Let A denote a direct or inverse Hessian approximation, or the Jacobian of a nonlinear system. A compact quasi-Newton representation encodes A with a low-rank matrix decomposition instead of storing an explicit full matrix. The resulting approximation is used in gradient-based optimization or nonlinear-system solution, with the compact form making large and constrained problems natural settings.

explainer.example: Consider minimizing a function with thousands of variables using a gradient-based method. Instead of forming a full matrix relating every variable to every other variable, the method keeps a low-rank decomposition of the inverse Hessian approximation and uses that representation when computing its optimization steps.

usedIn.name: Gradient-based optimization
usedIn.detail: Represents the Hessian approximation used to guide optimization steps.

usedIn.name: Nonlinear-system solving
usedIn.detail: Provides a compact low-rank representation of the system Jacobian.

usedIn.name: Large-scale problems
usedIn.detail: Avoids relying on an explicit full Hessian or Jacobian representation.

usedIn.name: Constrained optimization
usedIn.detail: Uses the same compact matrix representation in settings with constraints.

explainer.intuition: A full Hessian or Jacobian can be unwieldy when a problem is large. The compact representation keeps a low-rank decomposition of the needed approximation, preserving a useful matrix description without representing the full matrix directly.
howItWorks: Identify the matrix to approximate: a direct Hessian, an inverse Hessian, or a Jacobian.
Express that approximation using a low-rank matrix decomposition.
Keep the decomposition as the compact quasi-Newton representation.
Use the represented matrix in a gradient-based optimization algorithm or a nonlinear-system solve.
Apply the same approach to large-scale or constrained problems where a compact form is valuable.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives optimization and nonlinear-system methods a practical way to handle Hessian or Jacobian approximations in large problems. Its usefulness also extends to constrained optimization.
misconceptions: It is not limited to inverse Hessians; it can represent direct Hessians and Jacobians too.
It is a matrix representation, not a separate optimization objective.
Low-rank does not mean the underlying problem is small; the representation is often chosen for large problems.
